etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old English grasian (“to feed on grass”), from græs (“grass”).

definitions.definition: The act of grazing; a scratching or injuring lightly on passing.
A light abrasion; a slight scratch.
The act of animals feeding from pasture.

quote.text: If it be sundown, when the herds are returning from their daily graze in the long grass of the jungle, clouds of dust will be marking their track along every approach to the village  […]

definitions.definition: (transitive) To feed or supply (cattle, sheep, etc.) with grass; to furnish pasture for.

quote.citation: 1732 March 6 (Gregorian calendar; date written), [Jonathan Swift], Considerations upon Two Bills Sent Down from the R[ight] H[onourable] the H[ouse] of L[ords] to the H[onoura]ble H[ouse] of C[ommons of Ireland] Relating to the Clergy of I[relan]d, London:  […]  A. Moore, […], published 1732, →OCLC, page 24:
quote.text: He hath a Houſe and Barn in repair, a Field or tvvo to graze his Covvs, vvith a Garden and Orchard.
Although it is perfectly good meadowland, none of the villagers has ever grazed animals on the meadow on the other side of the wall.

definitions.definition: (transitive, intransitive) To feed on; to eat (growing herbage); to eat grass from (a pasture)

quote.citation: 1712 (date written), Alexander Pope, “Messiah. quote.text: Shylock: When Jacob grazed his uncle Laban's sheep

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To eat small  amounts of food periodically throughout the day, rather than at fixed mealtimes, often not in response to hunger.

quote.citation: 2008, Mohgah Elsheikh, Caroline Murphy, Polycystic Ovary Syndrome:
quote.text: Furthermore, people who take the time to sit down to proper meals find their food more satisfying than people who graze throughout the day. If you skip meals, you will inevitably end up snacking on more high-fat high-sugar foods.

quote.citation: 2018 July 24, Anahad O’Connor, “When We Eat, or Don’t Eat, May Be Critical for Health”, in The New York Times‎[1], →ISSN:
quote.text: Many people, however, snack and graze from roughly the time they wake up until shortly before they go to bed.

definitions.definition: To shoplift by consuming food or drink items before reaching the checkout.

quote.text: Grazing refers to customers who consume food items before paying for them, for example, a customer bags one and a half pounds of grapes in the produce department, eats some as she continues her shopping  […]

quote.citation: 2001, Labor Arbitration Information System, volume 2, page 59:
quote.text: Had the Grievant attempted to pay for the Mylanta or actually paid for it, then she would not be guilty of grazing or shoplifting.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To rub or touch lightly the surface of (a thing) in passing.

quote.citation: 1851 November 14, Herman Melville, chapter XXIII, in Moby-Dick; or, The Whale, 1st American edition, New York, N.Y.: Harper & Brothers; London: Richard Bentley, →OCLC:
quote.text: But in that gale, the port, the land, is that ship’s direst jeopardy; she must fly all hospitality; one touch of land, though it but graze the keel, would make her shudder through and through.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To cause a slight wound to; to scratch.
